notes: Virtual receiver only. Speeds, stopping and tracking values are rehearsal settings, not measured physical behavior.

Gains are the legacy collector's full tuned values (hold_kp at max_kp); unqualified for the guarded controller. The collector's 0.3 first-motion kp scale was used first and was too weak on the real arm: commands are position-only (no gravity or velocity feed-forward while collision envelopes are in force), so a joint's drive is hold_kp times its lead, and at 0.3 J2 and J3 (3.2 and 1.9 Nm at the lead limit) could not lift the arm, J1 followed at about 0.11 rad/s, and the wrists stalled on friction (J5 2.4 Nm/rad held 0.063 rad off target by 0.15 Nm). The operator chose the full gains on 2026-09-27: more force on contact (J2 17.6 Nm before its tracking bound), with collision checks still advisory.
J6 holds at 8 Nm/rad, above the collector's 3: at 3 its drive at the lead limit (0.14 Nm) did not break its friction, and it did not move in the first live sessions.

Each leader channel's hand-swept range (Helm Leaders tab) scales straight onto its robot joint's whole usable range. Arm joints scale from the operator-set leader zero (mapped onto the robot's reference pose) with one scale for both directions, sized so both robot ends are reached; past a robot limit the leader goes on and the robot holds.

Grippers touch and hold objects: no margin, no stopping reserve, no braking (a stop keeps the last target) and no tracking-error fault; effort and gain limits still bound them. They run at 10 rad/s over their whole range.

Speed caps follow the leader-to-robot scale: the wrist swivels (J5) map about 1.2-2 rad of leader travel onto about 4.6 rad, so they run at 2.5 rad/s. The elbows (J3, scale up to about 1.3) run at 1.2 rad/s with a harder stop (25 rad/s2) and a 0.05 rad tracking bound, which keeps their stopping reserve, and so their usable range, the same as at 0.8 rad/s. A command leads its measured position by at most 60% of the joint's tracking bound (position-only commands: a servo lags by hold_kd * speed / hold_kp, and a lead at the whole bound faulted J4 on a quick leader motion in the first live session), so the lead limit caps a joint's speed at 0.6 * bound / 40 ms before its speed cap where that is lower.

An arm route sign says whether the leader angle and the robot's CAD joint angle increase together; a gripper route sign of +1 means the leader angle increasing opens the gripper. Signs are candidates until verified in Helm.

Collision checks are advisory: the conservative keep-out bound only certifies about +/-0.011 rad per arm joint at the hanging pose (about 0.03 rad/s). Each cycle is still checked and shown in Helm; the virtual receiver is not blocked. Physical teleop needs a tighter, still-sound bound and enforced checks.

live.note: Live teleop drives one arm at a time on its physical motors, with advisory collision checks, until a two-arm collision bound exists; the other arm is never enabled. Each session starts from the reference pose (arms straight down, grippers closed). The motion settings below are unqualified: attended tests only, with the foot switch in reach.

sweep.note: The servo sweep (Helm's Tune tab, control/servo_sweep.py) steps each joint's stiffness from kp_ceiling down (default: its current hold gain), damping ratios, then speeds up to its speed cap (speed_ceiling raises a joint's cap for the sweep, at the cost of usable range: the receiver's collision reserve is taken at the cap). Defaults are in servo_sweep.DEFAULTS. The wrists and grippers get headroom: friction held J5 and J6 off target at their collector gains, and the first J6 sweep (2026-09-27) passed only its top rung, 16, so the wrists go to 24. bound_ceiling and speed_ceiling let the sweep set a joint's tracking bound and speed cap from its measurements (never lowered, and only while its usable range stays at least usable_floor of its swept travel): the light distal joints only (operator's choice, 2026-09-27); J1-J3 keep theirs until gravity and velocity feed-forward.
